incidents.title: CVE-2026-20079 — max-severity Cisco Secure FMC auth bypass exploited by Sandworm and Qilin to drop web shells
incidents.summary: Cisco confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-20079, a CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass in Secure Firewall Management Center's web interface that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker execute scripts and commands as root. Cisco Talos tracked three distinct post-compromise clusters — UAT-12197, UAT-11823, and UAT-11988 — with UAT-12197 dropping a JSP web shell into the FMC's Tomcat webroot that decodes a parameter and loads a Java class into the running process, alongside a JAR-based command executor and credential exfiltration; reporting attributes exploitation to both Sandworm and Qilin-linked activity. CISA added it to KEV as part of a Sep 10 batch with Cisco NetScaler and Fortinet, setting a Sep 12 federal patch deadline. Durable catch: any unexpected .jsp file appearing in an FMC's Tomcat webroot, or an unfamiliar JAR file sitting alongside it, is a near-certain sign of this specific exploitation chain — check that path first, before broader log review.
facts: CVE-2026-20079 CVSS 10.0 · UNAUTH ROOT VIA WEB INTERFACE
3 TALOS-TRACKED CLUSTERS: UAT-12197, UAT-11823, UAT-11988
ATTRIBUTED TO SANDWORM AND QILIN-LINKED ACTIVITY
incidents.action: Patch Secure Firewall Management Center to the fixed release immediately; inspect the Tomcat webroot for unexpected .jsp files and adjacent JAR files; review audit logs for authentication events tied to the related static-credential issue (CVE-2026-20316); rotate any credentials that may have transited a compromised FMC instance.

iocs.context: Cisco Secure FMC web-interface authentication bypass enabling unauthenticated root command execution, CVSS 10.0

iocs.value: Unexpected .jsp web shell in the FMC Tomcat webroot, paired with an unfamiliar JAR-based command executor
iocs.context: UAT-12197 post-exploitation artifact per Cisco Talos

incidents.title: CVE-2026-19490 — second Citrix NetScaler auth-bypass flaw in weeks, 56 honeypot exploit attempts recorded
incidents.summary: A second Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway authentication bypass, CVE-2026-19490 (CVSS 9.3), affects appliances configured as AAA virtual servers or Gateways running SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN, or RDP Proxy — the same appliance roles hit by CVE-2026-8452 weeks earlier. CISA added it to KEV Sep 10 in the same batch as the Cisco FMC and Fortinet flaws; honeypot telemetry recorded 56 exploitation attempts since Sep 3, with 36 of those on Sep 8 alone, showing exploitation intensified sharply once the flaw became public rather than trickling in gradually. Durable catch: NetScaler AAA/Gateway appliances have now had two independent KEV-listed auth-bypass flaws in the same short window — treat any unpatched NetScaler appliance from either disclosure as compromised rather than merely exposed, given how fast exploitation ramped after each one went public.
facts: CVE-2026-19490 CVSS 9.3 · AAA/GATEWAY AUTH BYPASS
56 HONEYPOT EXPLOIT ATTEMPTS SINCE SEP 3 · 36 IN A SINGLE DAY (SEP 8)
SECOND KEV-LISTED NETSCALER AUTH-BYPASS FLAW IN WEEKS (AFTER CVE-2026-8452)
incidents.action: Patch NetScaler ADC/Gateway to the fixed release addressing CVE-2026-19490 immediately; treat any appliance that was unpatched between disclosure and patch application as a probable target given the honeypot attempt volume; review AAA/Gateway authentication logs for anomalies since Sep 3.

iocs.context: Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway AAA/Gateway authentication bypass, CVSS 9.3

iocs.value: Exploitation attempts against NetScaler AAA/Gateway honeypots, concentrated Sep 3-8 (56 total, 36 on Sep 8 alone)
iocs.context: Observed exploitation intensity pattern

incidents.title: PivotC2 RAT campaign weaponizes FortiOS heap overflow against 3,000+ IPs, infects 178 devices
incidents.summary: A Russian-speaking-attributed campaign has been exploiting CVE-2025-25249, a heap-based buffer overflow in FortiOS, FortiSwitchManager, and FortiSASE (CVSS 7.3), to deliver the PivotC2 remote-access trojan via crafted requests, with exploitation evidence dating back to July 2026. CISA added it to KEV Sep 10 alongside the Cisco and Citrix flaws; the campaign has targeted over 3,000 IP addresses and successfully infected 178 devices, concentrated mostly in the United States, using shell scripts that drop exploit binaries and establish reverse shells via single-line Node.js commands. Durable catch: a compromised Fortinet device running an unfamiliar single-line Node.js process is PivotC2's specific reverse-shell mechanism — that process signature is more reliable to hunt for than the exploit request itself, since exploitation has been running undetected since July.
facts: CVE-2025-25249 CVSS 7.3 · HEAP OVERFLOW → PivotC2 RAT
3,000+ IPs TARGETED · 178 DEVICES INFECTED
EXPLOITATION DATES TO JULY 2026 · RUSSIAN-SPEAKING ACTOR ASSESSED
incidents.action: Patch FortiOS/FortiSwitchManager/FortiSASE to the fixed release for CVE-2025-25249 immediately; hunt for unfamiliar single-line Node.js processes on Fortinet appliances as PivotC2's reverse-shell mechanism; treat any device that was internet-facing and unpatched since July 2026 as potentially already infected regardless of current patch status.

iocs.context: FortiOS/FortiSwitchManager/FortiSASE heap-based buffer overflow enabling RCE, CVSS 7.3
Remote-access trojan delivered via exploitation of CVE-2025-25249

iocs.value: Reverse shell established via a single-line Node.js command on a Fortinet appliance
iocs.context: PivotC2 post-exploitation mechanism

incidents.title: 'StyleSmuggler' — CVE-2026-75650 lets attackers turn Adobe Commerce's own template engine into unauthenticated RCE
incidents.summary: Sansec disclosed CVE-2026-75650 ('StyleSmuggler'), a CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE affecting Adobe Commerce 2.4.4-2.4.9 and Magento Open Source 2.4.6-2.4.9, where an attacker injects PHP through Magento's email-template system by exploiting the fact that style properties are treated as harmless layout data and pass through template safeguards unchecked — the payload then rides Magento's own dependency-injection machinery into execution. Sansec observed active exploitation beginning Sep 4, three days before Adobe's out-of-band patch shipped Sep 7; CrowdSec has tracked 500 unique IPs sending matching requests since Sep 9, and 23 of the 410 addresses probing StyleSmuggler also tried last year's SessionReaper flaw (CVE-2025-54236) — the same actor set revisiting Magento. Durable catch: exploitation began three days before a patch existed — any Magento/Adobe Commerce store that applied hotfix VULN-39341 without also checking for a planted backdoor from that pre-patch window should assume compromise, not just apply the fix and move on.
facts: CVE-2026-75650 CVSS 10.0 · UNAUTH RCE VIA EMAIL TEMPLATE ENGINE
EXPLOITED FROM SEP 4, 3 DAYS BEFORE PATCH (SEP 7)
CROWDSEC: 500 UNIQUE IPs SINCE SEP 9 · 23/410 OVERLAP WITH SESSIONREAPER PROBING
incidents.action: Apply hotfix VULN-39341 immediately, then scan the store for backdoors planted during the Sep 4-7 pre-patch exploitation window rather than assuming the hotfix alone resolves prior compromise; review email-template configuration for unauthorized modifications; block or heighten monitoring on IPs previously seen probing SessionReaper (CVE-2025-54236) given the documented actor overlap.

iocs.context: Adobe Commerce/Magento email-template engine injection, unauthenticated RCE, CVSS 10.0
Out-of-band fix released Sep 7, 2026

iocs.value: Requests matching the StyleSmuggler exploitation pattern; 500 unique source IPs observed since Sep 9, with documented overlap against IPs that also probed CVE-2025-54236 (SessionReaper)
iocs.context: CrowdSec-tracked exploitation telemetry

incidents.title: CVE-2026-85706 — max-severity GitLab path traversal in the commits API added to KEV under emergency directive
incidents.summary: GitLab's repository commits API has an improper path-confinement and missing-authentication flaw, CVE-2026-85706 (CVSS 10.0), that lets an unauthenticated attacker read arbitrary files from an affected self-managed GitLab server under certain conditions. CISA added it to KEV Sep 11 with confirmed active-exploitation evidence, invoking emergency federal directive BOD 26-04 requiring immediate patching outside the normal cycle rather than the standard deadline window. GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated were already patched before disclosure; affected self-managed versions span 18.7 through 19.3.1. No public IOCs (attacker IPs, request signatures) accompanied the advisory. Durable catch: an unauthenticated arbitrary-file-read against a self-managed GitLab instance can pull CI/CD secrets, SSH keys, or config files straight off the server — treat this as a credential-exposure incident requiring rotation, not just a patch-and-move-on vulnerability.
facts: CVE-2026-85706 CVSS 10.0 · UNAUTH ARBITRARY FILE READ VIA COMMITS API
CISA INVOKED EMERGENCY DIRECTIVE BOD 26-04 (IMMEDIATE PATCH, NOT STANDARD DEADLINE)
AFFECTS SELF-MANAGED 18.7-19.3.1 · GITLAB.COM/DEDICATED ALREADY PATCHED
incidents.action: Patch self-managed GitLab to 19.1.8, 19.2.6, or 19.3.2 immediately per CISA's emergency directive; rotate any secrets, SSH keys, or credentials that were readable via the filesystem on an affected instance prior to patching; audit commits-API access logs for anomalous file-path requests.

iocs.context: GitLab repository commits API path traversal enabling unauthenticated arbitrary file read, CVSS 10.0
Fixed releases for self-managed instances

incidents.title: CVE-2026-86218 — pre-auth RCE in N-able N-central RMM exploited, fourth patch in five weeks
incidents.summary: N-able confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-86218 (CVSS 10.0), a static code injection flaw (CWE-96) in N-central that lets an unauthenticated attacker send crafted requests the server evaluates without validation, executing arbitrary OS commands as root with no authentication or user interaction required. Because N-central is an RMM platform used by managed service providers, a compromised instance is a foothold into every downstream endpoint that MSP manages, not just the N-central server itself; researchers note it can potentially be chained with two authentication-bypass flaws (CVE-2026-86206, CVE-2026-86207) to bypass console auth and create attacker-controlled admin accounts. CISA added it to KEV Sep 8; it was patched in N-central 2026.3 Hotfix 4 on Sep 5, marking N-able's fourth patch to the product in five weeks. Durable catch: N-central's role as an RMM makes this a supply-chain-shaped vulnerability — any MSP running an unpatched instance should assume every client endpoint it manages is in the blast radius, not just the RMM server.
facts: CVE-2026-86218 CVSS 10.0 · UNAUTH PRE-AUTH RCE AS ROOT
4TH N-CENTRAL PATCH IN 5 WEEKS
CHAINABLE WITH CVE-2026-86206/86207 FOR ADMIN ACCOUNT CREATION
incidents.action: Patch N-central to 2026.3 Hotfix 4 or later immediately; MSPs should audit for unauthorized admin accounts created via the CVE-2026-86206/86207 chain and treat any client endpoint managed through an unpatched instance as potentially exposed; review N-central access logs for crafted requests predating the patch.

iocs.context: N-able N-central static code injection, unauthenticated pre-auth RCE as root, CVSS 10.0
Fixed release

incidents.title: Microsoft's record 964-CVE Patch Tuesday includes two actively exploited Windows zero-days
incidents.summary: Microsoft's September Patch Tuesday addressed 964 CVEs — a record volume — including two zero-days confirmed exploited in the wild: CVE-2026-81963, an improper link-resolution ('link following') flaw in the Windows Update Stack that is the first such component to be exploited as a zero-day since 2022, and CVE-2026-85880, a heap-based buffer overflow in Windows ALPC. Both are elevation-of-privilege bugs rated CVSS 7.8 that let an attacker with initial local access escalate to SYSTEM, turning an initial foothold into full device control; CISA added both to KEV Sep 8 with a Sep 22 federal remediation deadline. No public IOCs (samples, attacker groups) were disclosed alongside either advisory. Durable catch: both zero-days require local access to start — they're the second stage of an intrusion that began another way, so patching them closes the escalation path but doesn't address however the attacker got a foothold in the first place.
facts: CVE-2026-81963 (WINDOWS UPDATE STACK) · CVE-2026-85880 (WINDOWS ALPC) · BOTH CVSS 7.8
FIRST WINDOWS UPDATE STACK ZERO-DAY EXPLOITED SINCE 2022
964 TOTAL CVEs PATCHED · RECORD VOLUME FOR A SINGLE PATCH TUESDAY
incidents.action: Apply September 2026 Windows cumulative updates immediately to close both elevation-of-privilege zero-days; since both require existing local access, prioritize investigating how attackers are gaining initial footholds (phishing, exposed RDP, etc.) rather than treating the patch alone as sufficient; meet the Sep 22 federal KEV remediation deadline where applicable.

iocs.context: Windows Update Stack link-following and Windows ALPC heap overflow, both local privilege escalation to SYSTEM, CVSS 7.8

incidents.kind: DATA BREACH · UTILITY · GUEST BILL PAY
incidents.title: CenterPoint Energy investigates alleged 7.49 million-record breach tied to its guest bill-pay feature
incidents.summary: A threat actor using the alias '4d722e4d656f77' posted on an open forum Sep 1 claiming theft of a CenterPoint Energy customer database containing 7.49 million raw records (6.73 million after filtering) — names, phone numbers, service/billing addresses, account and premise IDs, billing amounts, payment status, autopay/paperless settings, and partial Social Security numbers — and provided sample data to back the claim. Subsequent lawsuits allege the intrusion window ran Aug 17-Sep 1 and point specifically at CenterPoint's online guest bill-pay feature as the likely weak point, though the company has not publicly confirmed the breach or its scope as of this writing. Durable catch: a 'guest' payment flow that doesn't require an account is, by definition, a path with weaker identity verification than the authenticated account system sitting next to it — any utility or biller offering guest bill-pay should audit that specific flow's access controls independently of its main login system.
facts: 7.49M RAW RECORDS CLAIMED (6.73M FILTERED) · SAMPLE DATA PROVIDED
GUEST BILL-PAY FEATURE IDENTIFIED AS LIKELY ENTRY POINT
COMPANY HAS NOT PUBLICLY CONFIRMED BREACH SCOPE AS OF THIS WRITING
incidents.action: CenterPoint Energy customers should monitor for phishing using the leaked billing/account details and consider a credit freeze given the partial-SSN exposure; utilities and billers offering an unauthenticated guest bill-pay flow should audit that path's access controls and rate limiting specifically, since it's the suspected entry point here; watch for the company's own confirmation to establish verified scope.

iocs.context: Individual who posted the claimed CenterPoint Energy database for sale on an open forum

iocs.value: Unauthorized access via the online guest bill-pay feature (per subsequent litigation, not yet confirmed by CenterPoint)
iocs.context: Suspected entry point for the claimed breach

incidents.title: Veradigm discloses patient data breach after The Gentlemen ransomware gang claims 3.5 million records via vendor API
incidents.summary: Healthcare technology firm Veradigm disclosed that stolen login credentials within a third-party vendor's environment granted unauthorized access to a Veradigm API used for service delivery, which the attacker used to download patient records; Veradigm says the breach was contained to that vendor-facing interface with no disruption to internal systems and no clinical/medical data exposed. The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service gang added Veradigm to its leak site Sep 5, claiming 3.5 million patient records including names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and other PII, including Social Security numbers for a subset of customers. Durable catch: the attacker never touched Veradigm's own network — stolen vendor credentials against a narrow, purpose-built API endpoint were sufficient to reach 3.5 million patient records, which is the actual lesson for any organization exposing a vendor-facing API scoped to 'just' service delivery.
facts: 3.5M PATIENT RECORDS CLAIMED BY THE GENTLEMEN (LEAK SITE POST SEP 5)
INITIAL ACCESS: STOLEN VENDOR CREDENTIALS AGAINST A VERADIGM SERVICE API
SSNs INCLUDED FOR A SUBSET OF CUSTOMERS · NO CLINICAL DATA EXPOSED PER VENDOR
incidents.action: Veradigm-affiliated customers and patients should watch for identity-theft/phishing risk given the SSN exposure for a subset of records; organizations exposing vendor-facing APIs should scope and monitor those endpoints as tightly as customer-facing ones, since narrow API access was sufficient here to reach millions of records; require MFA on all vendor-facing service accounts, not just customer-facing logins.

iocs.context: Group claiming the Veradigm patient-data theft via a compromised third-party vendor

incidents.title: The Gentlemen ransomware claims Air Canada, alleges 51,409 critical files taken
incidents.summary: TheGentlemen ransomware group claimed a cyberattack against Air Canada Sep 9, alleging exfiltration of over 51,409 critical files and disrupting parts of the airline's operations — the second major claim from the same group within a week, following its Sep 5 listing of healthcare vendor Veradigm. Coverage of the claim notes the standard caveat for leak-site postings: the file count could be genuine, recycled from an earlier incident, exaggerated, or fabricated, and Air Canada has not independently confirmed the scope. Durable catch: two Gentlemen claims against unrelated sectors (healthcare vendor, airline) four days apart shows the group is running high-volume opportunistic claims rather than sector-targeted campaigns — the specific number of files claimed matters less than confirming initial access and containment independently of the leak-site post.
facts: 51,409 CRITICAL FILES CLAIMED · CANADA'S LARGEST AIRLINE
SECOND THEGENTLEMEN CLAIM IN A WEEK (AFTER VERADIGM, SEP 5)
CLAIM UNVERIFIED · AIR CANADA HAS NOT CONFIRMED SCOPE
incidents.action: Air Canada customers/partners should watch for official confirmation before treating the 51,409-file claim as verified; airlines and other high-profile targets should assume opportunistic ransomware groups will claim attacks regardless of actual access depth, and should have a rapid-verification process to confirm or refute leak-site claims quickly; monitor TheGentlemen's leak site for any proof files substantiating this listing.

iocs.context: Group claiming both the Air Canada and Veradigm incidents within the same week

incidents.title: AUDIT TEAM extortion group claims four victims across South Korea, Germany, and Argentina
incidents.summary: A data-extortion group operating under the name AUDIT TEAM claimed four victim organizations spanning South Korea, Germany, and Argentina in the second week of September, per AhnLab's weekly dark-web tracking. As with most fresh extortion-group listings, no victim has publicly confirmed the claims and no technical indicators (initial access vector, malware family, sample data) have been disclosed for any of the four. Durable catch: a newly visible extortion brand claiming victims across three countries and continents in a single week is either an established access broker relabeling old intrusions under a new name, or a genuinely fast-moving new operation — either way, the geographic and sector spread argues against assuming any one victim profile is exempt.
facts: 4 VICTIMS CLAIMED · SOUTH KOREA, GERMANY, ARGENTINA
NO TECHNICAL IOCs DISCLOSED FOR ANY LISTING
NAME/BRAND APPEARS NEWLY ACTIVE THIS WEEK PER ASEC TRACKING

sources.label: ASEC — Ransom & Dark Web Issues, Week 2 September 2026

incidents.action: Organizations in South Korea, Germany, and Argentina across any sector should treat AUDIT TEAM as an active, geographically opportunistic extortion group and review common ransomware entry points; monitor AUDIT TEAM's leak site for proof files that would substantiate any of the four claims before treating them as confirmed.

iocs.value: AUDIT TEAM (data-extortion group, newly active Sep 2026)
iocs.context: Group claiming four victims across South Korea, Germany, and Argentina

incidents.title: LAPSUS$ resumes activity, teases a new victim disclosure without naming a target
incidents.summary: AhnLab's weekly dark-web tracking flagged renewed LAPSUS$ activity in the second week of September, with the group teasing an upcoming victim disclosure without naming a target as of this writing. The group, part of the broader Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters collective that has been rebuilding under a brokered-access operational model after 2022-2023 law-enforcement arrests, has no confirmed new victim, technique, or technical indicator tied to this specific tease yet — it is a signal to watch rather than a confirmed incident. Durable catch: LAPSUS$'s historical playbook runs through social engineering against help desks and MFA fatigue rather than software exploits — any organization seeing this resurgence news should re-verify help-desk identity-verification procedures now, before a named victim (possibly their own environment) surfaces.
facts: GROUP TEASED A NEW VICTIM DISCLOSURE, NO TARGET NAMED YET
PART OF THE BROADER SCATTERED LAPSUS$ HUNTERS RESURGENCE
NO CONFIRMED VICTIM OR TECHNIQUE FOR THIS SPECIFIC TEASE

sources.label: ASEC — Ransom & Dark Web Issues, Week 2 September 2026

incidents.action: Re-verify help-desk and IT-support identity-verification procedures against social-engineering/vishing pretexts, LAPSUS$'s historical primary technique; move privileged accounts to phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) rather than push-based approval; monitor for the group's promised victim disclosure to confirm scope and technique once named.

iocs.value: LAPSUS$ / Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters (resurgent social-engineering-focused group)
iocs.context: Group teasing a new, unnamed victim disclosure

incidents.kind: DATA BREACH · HR DATA · MEDICAL DEVICE MANUFACTURER
incidents.title: Elixir Medical discloses HR data breach affecting current and former employees, two-month gap before detection
incidents.summary: Elixir Medical Corporation determined that an unauthorized party accessed its network Jul 20-21, 2026, but did not identify until Aug 11 that the accessed files contained sensitive HR information on current and former employees, consultants, and some of their beneficiaries and dependents — including Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, payment card data, medical information, and direct deposit bank account details. The company reported the breach to the California Attorney General Sep 4 and notified affected individuals; no technical details of the initial intrusion method have been disclosed. Durable catch: a three-week gap between initial access (Jul 20-21) and detection of what was actually taken (Aug 11) is the real story here — HR/finance data with SSNs, driver's licenses, and bank details sitting in a network segment that took weeks to fully scope after an intrusion was already known.
facts: INTRUSION JUL 20-21 · SCOPE OF HR DATA ACCESS NOT CONFIRMED UNTIL AUG 11
SSNs, DRIVER'S LICENSES, PAYMENT CARD DATA, DIRECT-DEPOSIT BANK DETAILS EXPOSED
REPORTED TO CALIFORNIA AG SEP 4 · NO INTRUSION-VECTOR TECHNICAL DETAILS DISCLOSED
incidents.action: Affected current/former Elixir Medical employees and dependents should place a credit freeze given the SSN, driver's license, and bank-account exposure; organizations should audit how long it takes to fully scope data accessed after an intrusion is detected, since the gap between access and understanding impact was the operative failure here, not just the initial access itself.

iocs.value: Unauthorized network access to HR/finance file stores containing SSNs, driver's license numbers, payment card, and direct-deposit bank data
iocs.context: Scope of the confirmed breach
